rationale: Repair of rejected trial-recovered-19ccfe875f on the same selected boundary (joint groups ef1a650b08785209a023/92f04768733eb2543f5d/4a79f0c7bb426e51060b, the 145 prefill-phase Qwen3RMSNorm module sites). Measured rejection cause (previous-feedback.txt + observations/previous-after/candidate_diagnostics-4123e6d6.json): that candidate replaced each forward with aten::_fused_rms_norm(...)[0] behind a torch.allclose(atol=rtol=0.02) per-site gate; all 145 gates passed (routes fused-rms-norm-gated x1 then fused-rms-norm), yet output.logits failed both continuous steps with 1884096/4861952 elements (38.8%) mismatched and max abs 4.09375 - one flipped greedy token (~step 20) with full trajectory divergence after it. Root cause, verified on the measured worker's interpreter (torch 2.13.0+cu129 CPU): _fused_rms_norm multiplies the weight in fp32 with a single bf16 rounding, while transformers 5.16.1 rounds the normalized activation to bf16 before the bf16 weight multiply; the formulas differ by up to 1 bf16 ulp per element (0.0078 at unit scale). A 0.02 per-layer gate accepts exactly that drift, which propagates through 36 layers into the KV cache and per-step logits, and require_exact_greedy_tokens rejects a single near-tie argmax flip. The gate's tolerance scale was the defect; the launch-fusion idea was sound. This repair keeps the numerically order-sensitive part of the parent chain in aten and fuses only arithmetic that is identical operation-for-operation: the fp32 square tensor feeding the unchanged aten::mean.dim reduction, and the elementwise tail mul->to.bf16->weight-mul, whose equivalence to aten's kernels (correctly-rounded fp32 multiplies plus round-to-nearest-even bf16 casts, no fusion across a rounding boundary, single fp32 product of two bf16 values is exact) was verified bit-exact on the worker interpreter over randomized bf16 inputs. Each site is gated on its first live invocation by a BITWISE torch.equal against the parent output on the same input (plus a bitwise compare of the fp32 square tensor against the parent's to.f32+pow for the Triton-square levels, closing the sub-bf16 absorption hole). A ladder negotiates the most fused level that is bitwise-identical on this GPU/torch build: L1 = Triton square + aten mean + one Triton tail kernel computing rsqrt(m+eps), scale and weight multiply (8 kernels -> 3); L2 = Triton square + aten mean/add/rsqrt + Triton tail (5 kernels); L3 = parent's own to.f32/pow/mean/add/rsqrt + Triton tail (6 kernels, relies only on the provably-exact tail); any mismatch, compile or runtime failure permanently routes that site to the parent with a concise route label. Bitwise-equal prefill activations give a bitwise-equal KV cache, logits and greedy tokens, so the frozen checks see the parent's own outputs. Expected effect from measured per-call kernel times (target-resources.json, rank 0): the 145 sites cost 2657.7 us of CUDA kernel time in the TTFT window (73x19.39 us [1,256,2560], 36x21.41 us [1,256,32,128], 36x13.09 us [1,256,8,128], 8 kernels each: to.f32 2.98, pow 2.18, reduce 4.80, add 0.99, rsqrt 1.02, mul 2.91, to.bf16 1.66, wmul 2.91 us on the big norm). L1 removes ~5 of 8 kernels and the fp32 intermediate z (5.2 MB) and bf16 intermediate b (2.6 MB) per [1,256,2560] call, plausibly 0.7-1.4 ms of the 24.44 ms ttft, with fewer launch-bound kernels also shrinking stream gaps; the honest AB/BA measurement decides, and the fallback ladder guarantees fidelity regardless of which level engages. Decode is untouched: no decode-phase RMSNorm sites exist in targets.json and the signature guard admits only each site's observed prefill signature. Composition with installed bundle trial-fc57bca7b9-param-f71a7c8a is preserved: while its CUDA-graph capture attempt is active the gate defers (comparison must synchronize) and the parent chain serves the call, so capture records parent kernels; after gating, already-compiled Triton kernels launch capture-safely. On this worker that capture aborts at the first SDPA call ('No available kernel', measured route parent-fallback:setup-failure:flash-dispatch-refused) and prefill runs eagerly, which is exactly where these replacements act.
setup_work: No parameter mutation, no weight transforms, no captured graphs, no retained pools, nothing fixture-dependent cached. Lazy setup happens once per site on the first live (non-capturing) invocation, which lands in the untimed quality/reference phase before warmup and repeats: (1) Triton JIT compilation of two small kernels, at most one specialization per normalized size (2560 and 128) per level variant actually reached - 3-5 compiles of ~1 s each across the whole run, shared by all sites via the JIT cache; (2) the bitwise gate runs the parent chain plus the candidate chain and two torch.equal comparisons per site (level preference is memoized per normalized size, so later sites usually gate on the first attempt); total one-time gate cost is on the order of tens of ms. Timed invocations then execute 3-6 kernels per norm instead of 8 and allocate 2-3 intermediates instead of 6-8, so per-run peak_allocated_bytes inside the norm chain decreases or stays equal; no lifecycle memory claim is made beyond that.
quality_risks: A Triton codegen difference on this GPU (e.g., tl.rsqrt not matching aten rsqrt, or a different bf16 conversion rounding) makes a level fail its bitwise gate; the site then uses a lower level or the parent, costing speedup but never output fidelity.

The bitwise gate runs on one live input per site; it verifies implementations, not all future data. The fused arithmetic is elementwise IEEE multiplication plus RNE casts with the reduction kept in aten, so data-dependence of the result is exactly the parent's; the s-level bitwise check additionally pins the variance path. Residual risk is a compiler bug that is input-dependent on values not present at gating - not observed and structurally unlikely for elementwise ops.

If every level fails on every site (e.g., Triton unavailable in the worker process), all 145 sites delegate to the parent and the measured gain is zero; the AB measurement then honestly rejects the candidate instead of the quality gate.

Triton's Python-side launch overhead (~2-5 us) partially offsets the removed aten launches on the small launch-bound q_norm/k_norm sites; if net kernel-time savings fall below the 0.14 ms paired noise bound the AB/BA measurement rejects the candidate on speed, not quality.

require_exact_greedy_tokens is protected by construction here: unlike the rejected single-rounding fused op, every engaged level is bit-identical to the parent on the gated live input, and decode-phase sites are not replaced at all.
